Aim To assess the value of a new marker H-FABP in the blood in patients with suspected coronary syndrome, H-FABP at 12-24 hours from onset of symptoms would identify patients at risk of long term adverse outcomes more accurately than troponin.  In conjunction with H-FABP, the researcher will measure another marker brain-type natriuretic peptide (BNP)  All cause mortality at 6 months Secondary outcome measures include cardiovascular mortality and reinfarction
